notes.6: Question 6 was answered correctly by 35% who chose option B. 12% chose option A, 6% chose option C and 47% chose option D. Option D would increase the supply and cause the supply curve to shift, any change in demand would be represented as a movement along the existing demand curve. Options A and C would shift the demand curve in the opposite direction to that shown on the diagram.
notes.18: Question 18 was answered correctly by 34% who chose option D. 18% chose option A, 17% chose option B and 31% chose option C. When the tax is imposed the new equilibrium quantity would be Q and the new price T. The government would receive TUZY. Compared with the original price (V) the consumer would pay part of the tax (TUWV – option C) but the producer also has to pay part of the tax. Options A and B involve the original quantity (E) which becomes irrelevant.
notes.25: Question 25 was answered correctly by 24% of the candidates who chose option B. 67% chose option A, and 9% chose option D. No candidate chose option C. The level of Gross Domestic Product (option A) is a misleading indicator of development because it does not take account of the population of the country. Of the options given the migration to the urban areas where there are more opportunities for employment is the most helpful indicator.
notes.general_comments: The questions for which most candidates selected the correct answer were 3, 5, 7, 11, and 19. These questions were answered correctly by 80% or more of the candidates. They covered different parts of the syllabus and were set to test different skills. The questions for which the fewest candidates selected the correct answer were 6, 18, and 25. These questions were answered correctly by 40% or fewer candidates. The rest of the questions gave results which were well within the levels expected.
